articles.title: 5 reasons Deion Sanders and Colorado might actually be good in 2026
articles.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders has said he has a 'pretty good football team' this year and his best coaching staff ever. He might actually be right.
articles.body:
Before he started his third season at Colorado in 2025, coach Deion Sanders proclaimed he had assembled his best team ever .

Then the Buffaloes finished with a 3-9 record .

This year, he says he has a " pretty good football team " along with his " best coaching staff " ever.

College football season predictions: Picks for CFP, Heisman, biggest surprises

The experts and oddsmakers don't and are picking his team to finish near the bottom of the Big 12 .

But I do believe him and am picking Colorado to finish among the top 3 in the league, along with Texas Tech and BYU. Here are five reasons as the Buffs prepare to open the season Thursday, Sept. 3 at Georgia Tech (8 p.m. ET; ESPN).

Sanders deserves credit for innovating and adjusting in the age of unlimited annual player transfers. He was the first transfer portal king in 2023 before it was considered cool in college football. This year, he entered the summer with 41 new scholarship transfers from other four-year colleges, including 23 from outside the Power Four conferences, according to CU records.

In a change from before, Sanders favored production over potential with this group, much like Indiana did last year on its run to the national championship. Of those 23 transfers from the lower rungs of Division I, 16 are former starters.

That list doesn't even count wide receiver transfer Kam Perry, a walk-on who started 12 games last year at Miami (Ohio) and made 43 catches for 976 yards.

2. Offensive coordinator Brennan Marion has the edge

Marion is Sanders' third offensive coordinator in four seasons but also the edgiest since the Buffs shocked the nation with a 3-0 start under then-offensive coordinator Sean Lewis in 2023.

Marion's Go-Go offense is eclectic enough to spin the heads of opposing defenses and has averaged at least 33 points per game since 2023, when he was offensive coordinator at UNLV.

His background and leadership pedigree also make him a potential successor to Sanders someday, continuing the upward climb he's been making ever since he was homeless in junior college and slept under the bleachers of the stadium .

Colorado started three quarterbacks last year, which is another way of saying they didn't have any good enough for Sanders. Lewis was one of those starters for two of those games but was only 18 years old as a touted freshman out of Georgia. This is his moment. He compiled a 39-4 record as a three-year starter in high school and has the potential to lead Colorado to a special season if he adjusts well to Marion's offense early on.

Marion has said Lewis has a " million-dollar arm " and especially wants to win the season opener in his home state.

"He understands how to win a football game," Marion said Aug. 27.

This time, he'll benefit from a big, beefy offensive line averaging well over 300 pounds apiece, plus a crew of talented receivers, including Texas transfer DeAndre Moore.

The Buffs made a clean break from last year, when they ranked 135 th out of 136 major college teams in rushing yards allowed per game with 222.5. They have a new defensive coordinator (Chris Marve), new cornerbacks coach ( Aaron Fletcher ), new defensive line coach (Dante Carter) and new safeties coach ( Vonn Bell ) to go with an all-new starting lineup. It features playmakers who have drawn raves, including Tennessee transfer defensive back Boo Carter and Notre Dame transfer cornerback Cree Thomas.

Sanders especially praised his linebackers, which include Texas transfer Liona Lefau.

"I can't say enough about them," Sanders said Aug. 14. "They're extraordinary. They're probably the best position group on this team."

Texas Tech once again has the best roster that money can buy in the Big 12. BYU also has the stars to compete for the Big 12 title, just like the Cougars did in 2024 and 2025. But after that, who really knows with so many players changing teams every year? Why not Colorado?

Sanders has been up and down in Boulder to the extreme — a 3-0 start in 2023, followed by a 1-8 finish, then a 9-4 season in 2024 and a 3-9 season in 2025. The prediction here is the pendulum is swinging back, especially with expectations so low now outside of Colorado.

On the other hand, what happens if the Buffs get crushed in their opener in Atlanta? Their season could plunge downhill from there with two of their next three games on the road. But a win there could have the opposite effect, and this team is too improved to let that happen anyway.

articles.title: Cowboys' Von Miller lands No. 40 by making Luepke a business partner
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboy recent acquisition Von Miller has No. 40, but he had to give Hunter Luepke more than a lifetime supply of chicken to get it.
articles.body:
The funniest subplot of the Dallas Cowboys' preseason has been resolved. Von Miller now owns No. 40 and Hunter Luepke owns part of a chicken farm.

Shortly after Dallas signed the free agent and future Hall of Famer Miller, he revealed he wanted to wear the No. 40 that he wore at DeSoto High School (Dallas area) and at Texas A&M, with the snag that it was already held by the fullback Luepke.

To that end Miller, the co-founder and co-owner of the organic poultry farm Greener Pastures Chicken, offered Luepke a lifetime supply of chicken . He may have underestimated Luepke's bargaining skills and now Luepke is evidently a business partner.

"Being the great negotiator he is, he was like, 'How about equity in Greener Pastures Chicken?'" Miller said on his Free Range podcast. "I was like, 'It's something that we could probably work out.' … 'We kind of had to do some negotiating at first. He's been 40 for a long time. It ain't something that I can just come in and Boss Hogg."

Miller said he was 90% certain he had a deal, and now it's 100%, official. Miller is in No. 40 and Luepke is moving to No. 30. This may come as a relief to anyone who bought a $150 Von Miller jersey . The amount of equity he received is undisclosed, but there is likely plenty of chicken in the future for both of them.

In other news, Caleb Downs is now officially in the No. 13 he has worn for most of the preseason.

articles.title: Yankees expected to make Brian Cashman job decision that should not be a surprise
articles.summary: The Yankees' front office exec seems like he's got a safe seat in New York.
articles.body:
As the 2026 season winds down, plenty of manager and front office positions are going to open around the league. Some are already open, and teams are looking to make some new hires.

But what about the New York Yankees ? They would obviously keep their power structure intact if they win the World Series, but in general, regardless of the season outcome, what are the Yankees most likely to do?

According to MLB insider Robert Murray of Fansided.com , the Yankees are expected to keep Brian Cashman, along with Aaron Boone, as both of their jobs are seemingly very safe regardless of the outcome of the 2026 Yankees season.

Yankees expected to keep Brian Cashman regardless of 2026 season outcome

"But both Cashman and Boone have done a very good job in New York. Cashman is a surefire Hall of Fame executive," Murray writes. "... I firmly expect both to remain with the Yankees beyond the 2026 season. They do not feel like they are in any danger of being let go."

The Yankees are currently contending for the AL East title, though the Tampa Bay Rays have a solid lead that, unless Aaron Judge returns from injury, might be too difficult to catch up to.

Cashman received some flak for bringing back a lot of their players this offseason, with the Trent Grisham qualifying offer decision also not being well received.

The same went for the trade deadline, as Cashman didn't exactly receive resounding praise for his addition of Heliot Ramos, and the lack of some extra bullpen help or a new catcher.

But the re-signing of Cody Bellinger, the trade for Ryan Weathers, and the trade for Luis Garcia Jr. at the MLB trade deadline were all great moves that have helped and will help the Yankees this season.

While there might be some Yankees fans frustrated with Cashman's roster construction, Murray wholeheartedly believes that Cashman isn't going to be leaving the Yankees now, or anytime soon.

Sure, he might've made some mistakes over the offseason, but every executive and general manager in every professional sports league does. Cashman has made mistakes, but he's more than made up for it with high-quality moves during his tenure.

Neither Cashman nor Boone is expected to be let go at the end of the season, according to Murray. This shouldn't surprise any Yankees fans, as Cashman is practically locked in as long as he wants the job.

articles.title: So, that J.J. McCarthy Trade Rumor Did Get an Answer (Sort Of)
articles.summary: Nolan Teasley was asked about possibly trading J.J. McCarthy. Given that it’s a pertinent topic, the question is a good […]
articles.body:
Nolan Teasley was asked about possibly trading J.J. McCarthy . Given that it's a pertinent topic, the question is a good one to ask (at least if you ask me).

Part of the problem is that Mr. Teasley didn't appear particularly keen about digging into the issue . His answer about whether teams had been calling: "That's something I'll probably keep internal. We get calls all the time but it's not something I would directly comment on [in] regards to any player." Teasley, in short, opts to keep his cards close to his chest. Maybe teams called; maybe teams didn't. All that he's saying is that front offices talk commonly about trades but he wouldn't go any further.

Does J.J. McCarthy Get Sent Packing Via Trade?

Of course, the possibility remains that Mr. McCarthy will get sent packing. Any trade needs a pair of partners to do business.

Presumably, there are teams out there willing to send out a draft pick(s) to snag the 23-year-old quarterback. The issue is simply that nobody in their right mind would hand over anything close to what the Vikings had to pay to get him in the first place: the No. 10 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft.

Minnesota can therefore hang onto the young fella or sell for pennies on the dollar.

In his column earlier today, Jeff Diamond wrote about the McCarthy trade issue .

"If another team offered a first round pick for McCarthy," Diamond writes, "it would be hard to pass up. That's certainly not going to happen after his injury-prone and inconsistent play last year (although he did end the season with better play and four straight wins) and in preseason this year with his accuracy still a major concern."

More from Diamond: "There's no way Teasley and O'Connell would trade McCarthy for the minimal return of probably a fourth round pick at this point (which is what the 49ers received from the Cowboys for Trey Lance in 2023 and Lance was the third overall pick in 2021 but was often hurt and inconsistent and he was beat out for the starting job by Brock Purdy)."

Similarly of note is the work of Tom Rudelius, a math nerd who ventured into the precedent of recent NFL history to gauge what J.J. McCarthy could demand on the trade market .

After spilling some digital ink, Rudelius writes that "it's hard to imagine that McCarthy could net more than a 5th Round pick at this point. Part of the reason why the price for former 1st Round QBs has dropped in recent years is probably because none of the QBs in the table above have brought any meaningful value to the team that traded for them."

Would Nolan Teasley move on from J.J. McCarthy if the offer involved recouping a 4th or 5th? That's a good question, but it's hard to know if there has even been some trade discussions happening at all.

In 2025, McCarthy went 6-4 as Minnesota's starting quarterback. Pushing his team to that winning record came despite completing a horrible 57.6% of his passes while only climbing up to 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns. Keep in mind that he had 12 interceptions alongside 6 fumbles.

At 23, J.J. McCarthy still has a lot of football in front of him. Whether that football gets played in the North Star State is an open question.

articles.title: Cowboys strip their best player of Captain's C, announce 2026 crew
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have voted for their new captains, but a top player isn't returning to the captain's chair.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys had a unique approach to their game-day captains under former head coach Mike McCarthy. Each week, the team would designate new captains, leading to many players holding the honor, but losing the weekly accountability from having season-long designations. Brian Schottenheimer changed that to a more traditional structure in his first season, naming two captains from each unit.

Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb were captains for the offense, Donovan Wilson and Osa Odighizuwa were captains for the defense, and Brandon Aubrey and CJ Goodwin wore the "C" for the special teams unit. Three of those players, Wilson, Odighizuwa and Goodwin, are no longer on the team, opening up the opportunity for new names to join the fold. But it's not the names which are added that are noteworthy; it's a name that's been removed.

Prescott is the sole designation for the offense, meaning that after sporting the C for all of 2025, Lamb is no longer one of the offense's captains. Whether or not this is a significant development is in the eyes of the beholder, but with the front office continuously chirping about their inability to pay top dollar for both Lamb and wideout George Pickens beyond this season, it's an interesting change.

To be clear, this isn't a coach's decision; the players vote on the captains each year.

Lamb, who was recently named the NFC East's best player by ESPN , has two years remaining on his contract beyond this one, while Pickens is playing on the franchise tag for 2026.

Meanwhile, the team has kept Aubrey as the special teams captain, and named the starting defensive interior as co-captains for the defense. Quinnen Williams, acquired in a deadline trade last year, received a hefty extension this year, cementing his role as the centerpiece of the defense moving forward. He's joined in the captain's room by Kenny Clark, the defense's elder statesman prior to the late-camp signing of Von Miller.

In a nutshell, the team voted for the players with the biggest paychecks and most responsibility from each unit, along with the returning player with the most skins on the wall.

articles.title: Ohio State hosting Jaxson Davis, Deng Ngor on official visits
articles.summary: As the first home football game of 2026 approaches, here's which 2027 prospects the Ohio State men's basketball team will host during the weekend.
articles.body:
During the first home football game at Ohio State this season, the Buckeyes men's basketball team will host two prospects on official visits.

When OSU hosts Ball State on Sept. 5 at Ohio Stadium, coach Jake Diebler will bring two players from the class of 2027 along for the experience.

It's still unclear how many players Ohio State might sign for its 2027 class. The Buckeyes had a commitment from five-star guard LJ Smith , but he graduated early and is getting his freshman season started with the Buckeyes. Of the 15 players currently on Ohio State's roster, the only one known to be out of eligibility after this season is fifth-year guard Jimmie Williams .

Otherwise, all 14 other players would have the ability to still be on the roster for 2027-28. Granted, that scenario is highly unlikely in the era of name, image and likeness rights, but it does decrease the likelihood of Ohio State signing a big 2027 class.

Here are the two prospects Ohio State will be hosting on official visits during the weekend of Aug. 4-6.

Listed at 6-foot, 165 pounds, Davis is a four-star point guard originally from Chicago who will play his senior season at Kansas City (Kansas) Monarch Academy. He is the No. 41 national prospect in the 247Sports.com composite, the No. 9 point guard in the country and the No. 1 player in Kansas.

This is expected to be the first of four visits for Davis. He is scheduled to go to Minnesota on Sept. 11, Iowa on Sept. 19 and Michigan State on Oct. 1.

The 6-8, 200-pound power forward has made a significant rise in the 247Sports recruiting rankings this summer. Ngor was listed as the No. 150 national prospect until late August, and when the rankings refreshed, he was up to No. 55.

A senior at Fort Erie (Ontario) International Academy, Ngor also has planned visits to see Washington on Sept. 18, Florida on Sept. 22 and Duke on Oct. 15.

articles.title: Newcastle United vs Bournemouth: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction
articles.summary: Newcastle vs Bournemouth Preview: Jaissle and Rose Face Early Premier League TestTwo games are a poor basis for grand conclusions, but they are enough to spo...
articles.body:
Newcastle vs Bournemouth Preview: Jaissle and Rose Face Early Premier League Test

Two games are a poor basis for grand conclusions, but they are enough to spot trends. Newcastle United look sharper, quicker and more coherent than plenty expected after a summer of change. Bournemouth have been competitive too, but they are still paying for late lapses. That is the backdrop to this Premier League meeting, a game that already feels useful in measuring where both clubs are heading.

There was understandable anxiety around Newcastle after major upheaval, particularly with Matthias Jaissle replacing Eddie Howe and several familiar names moving on. So far, the response has been strong. A 2-2 draw against Liverpool could easily have been more, then came a deserved 2-0 win away at Tottenham. That is not noise. That is evidence.

Bournemouth also changed direction in the dugout after Andoni Iraola left for Liverpool, with Marco Rose taking charge. The performances have had substance, the outcomes less so. A 2-1 defeat at Manchester City came after they led 1-0, and a 1-1 draw against Everton was spoiled by a late equaliser. It is the kind of start that leaves a manager encouraged by the process and irritated by the details.

Jaissle has injuries to deal with across the pitch. Dan Burn is out with an ankle and foot issue, Joelinton is sidelined by a thigh problem, and William Osula is also unavailable because of an ankle and foot injury. Tino Livramento has returned to training after calf surgery, but this match may come too soon.

That puts more focus on the midfield pairing. Nico Gonzalez started against Spurs and looks set to continue alongside Lewis Miley. It gives Newcastle control and legs in the middle, and right now that matters. Summer arrival Matias Fernandez-Pardo, signed from Lille, is expected to start on the bench, which is sensible rather than cautious.

Further forward, Newcastle have threat. Yoane Wissa has started the season well after an injury-hit first campaign at the club, and his goal at Spurs underlined why he can be central to this side. He is direct, he attacks space early, and he does not need much invitation.

Bournemouth's summer was defined more by retention than recruitment, and there is value in that. Keeping quality players matters. Alex Scott remains the reference point in midfield after scoring against Everton, and his job will be to feed Evanilson, with Marcus Tavernier, Justin Kluivert and Rayan operating behind him.

There are absentees here too. Junior Kroupi, Julian Araujo, Amine Adli and Veljko Milosavljevic remain unavailable. Even so, Rose has enough attacking quality to cause Newcastle problems, particularly if the game opens up in transition.

Tavernier is one to watch. He scored against Manchester City and may have penalty duties. In a match where both sides carry attacking intent, that matters.

This is a tough call because the margins have been thin for both clubs. Newcastle have looked the more convincing side through two matches, and they carry momentum after winning at Spurs. Bournemouth have enough craft and speed to score, but they keep leaving the door open.

So the blunt verdict is simple. Expect chances, expect spells of control from both teams, and expect this to be close.

articles.title: A closer look at newest Saints tight end Stone Smartt
articles.summary: New Saints practice squad tight end Stone Smartt has the versatility that could benefit the offense as a developmental project
articles.body:
One of the roster changes made by the New Orleans Saints since roster cutdowns on Sunday was adding another tight end. Fourth-year veteran Stone Smartt was a waiver claim by the Saints for their practice squad.

Awarded No. 84 upon his arrival, Smartt is joined on the practice squad by tight end Treyton Welch, re-signed by New Orleans on Wednesday. Here's a closer look at Smartt, the team's newest tight end.

New Orleans Saints at Dallas Cowboys: Best photos of preseason Week 3

A state championship quarterback at Del Oro High School in California, Smartt would be recruited to play quarterback at Northern Arizona. He'd transfer to River City Community College after one year with next to no action. After one year as a JUCO All-American, Smartt then transferred to Old Dominion. He was the quarterback for the Monarchs in 2019, completing 57.1% of his passes for 1,006 yards with 1 touchdown, 6 interceptions, and 181 rushing yards with another 5 scores. In 2021, Smartt moved to wide receiver. That year, he'd pull in 17 receptions for 167 yards.

Smartt was not selected in the 2022 NFL Draft, instead signing on with the Los Angeles Chargers. Head coach of the Chargers at that time was Brandon Staley, defensive coordinator for the Saints. Staley would coach Smartt into his second year with the Chargers. Offensive coordinator for the Chargers that second season in 2023 was Kellen Moore, now head coach of New Orleans.

As a rookie in 2022, Smartt appeared in seven games with one start, catching 4 passes for 17 yards. In 2023, he'd appear in 16 games with three starts, playing in what remains a career-best 309 offensive snaps. Smartt would have 11 receptions for 155 yards, catching his first career touchdown. He'd have 16 catches for 208 yards in 2024, his career-high in both categories to this point.

Smartt was signed by the New York Jets during 2025 free agency. He'd appear in 15 games and catch 7 balls for 52 yards. This offseason, Smartt was signed by the Philadelphia Eagles in free agency but released on Aug. 29. The Saints signed him three days later after roster cutdowns throughout the NFL.

Smartt is expected to start 2026 on the practice squad. New Orleans has three talented tight ends in Juwan Johnson, Noah Fant, and rookie Oscar Delp. However, Smartt may get a look on special teams at some because of his athleticism. He's played 445 snaps on the special teams units over the last three seasons. A former high school and college quarterback, Smartt also has some versatility to go along with his athletic skills that could be beneficial to the Saints offense as a developmental player.

articles.title: Blue Jays beat Guardians 6-3 to close within a half-game of the final AL wild-card spot
articles.summary: Brett Bateman had three hits, Nathan Lukes lined a two-run double with the bases loaded in the fifth inning and the Toronto Blue Jays moved within striking d...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — Brett Bateman had three hits, Nathan Lukes lined a two-run double with the bases loaded in the fifth inning and the Toronto Blue Jays moved within striking distance of the third AL wild-card spot with a 6-3 victory over the Cleveland Guardians on Thursday.

Toronto (70-71) has won five of six and is a half-game behind Cleveland (70-70) after taking two of three in the series. The Blue Jays also won four of six in the season series.

Tanner Bibee took a major league-leading 15th loss for the Guardians. Austin Hedges had a two-run, bases-loaded single in the fifth inning to get Cleveland within 5-3.

Angel Genao came up as the potential tying run with runners on first and second and two outs in the ninth, but Louis Varland struck him out to pick up his 32nd save in 33 opportunities. Spencer Miles (6-2) got the win.

The game was tied at 1 before Toronto sent 10 to the plate in its four-run fifth.

Ernie Clement and Brandon Valenzuela drew walks before Bateman got aboard with a bunt single down the third-base line to load the bases. Bibee (5-15) decided to make a play on the bunt, even though it appeared as if it was going to roll foul. Lukes then followed with the go-ahead hit.

Bibee, who gave up five runs on four hits, tied a career high with five walks in four-plus innings.

Toronto starter José Soriano allowed three runs on six hits in 4 2/3 innings.

Blue Jays: Head to Kansas City for a weekend series. RHP Jameson Taillon (2-6, 5.68 ERA) will start on Friday.

Guardians: Have a split doubleheader against Detroit on Friday to start a four-game set. Game 1's starter has not been determined. LHP Foster Griffin (15-4, 3.21 ERA) is expected to go in the nightcap.

articles.title: We want Fury v Joshua at Wembley - London mayor
articles.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in to...
articles.body:
London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.

BBC Sport understands Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office in recent weeks about bringing the long-awaited contest to the national stadium.

However, with organisers and broadcaster Netflix understood to favour New York's Madison Square Garden for a November bout, sources close to the discussions say talks over a London venue have not progressed, with no detailed talks over dates or timings.

"A message to the promoters - we want to host it in London. Talk to us, we're really keen to have it," Khan told BBC Sport on Thursday.

Wembley Stadium's usual curfew is 23:00, although Khan has previously indicated he would support efforts to bring the fight to London.

A late-night fight in London - potentially in the early hours - could mean it draws a larger television audience in the US.

Brent Council, the local authority involved in any approval, has said a potential extension of the curfew would need to be assessed by Wembley's safety advisory group.

It remains unclear how late that curfew could be pushed back.

"Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are two great British boxers. Both have been world champions," Khan said.

"They both recognise and love the fans in this country who have supported them throughout their careers, amateur and professional.

"Wembley has hosted many fantastic events, including bouts involving Tyson and Anthony. We, the fans, want to see them box live in London."

There is hope that the venue will be finalised in the coming days. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has said he wants an announcement this week, with a news conference to follow next week.

BBC Sport has contacted Sela for comment.

Hearn says his side signed a contract for the bout to take place in the United Kingdom, while Sela and Netflix's preference would be the United States, to cater for American audiences.

Matchroom Boxing's Hearn has previously said Joshua's contract specifically stipulated a UK venue and would need to be renegotiated for the fight to take place Stateside.

Hearn says he has since set out terms under which Matchroom would agree to the change, with negotiations continuing over a possible move to New York.

The contact from Sela represents a significant development from the end of July, when sources close to the mayor told BBC Sport there had been no approach from the fight's organisers.

But the lack of progress since that initial contact underlines the uncertainty still surrounding Wembley's chances of hosting the contest.

"I'm hoping the promoters understand that not only will you get 100,000 people watching this bout live, you'll get millions watching it across the globe, where both boxers are cheered on by their loyal fans," Khan said.
authors: Kal Sajad - BBC Sport boxing journalist

articles.title: Cubs Lose 1.85 Pitcher For Rest Of Season
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs have been waiting for Ben Brown to return, but his season is over
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs have been waiting for Ben Brown to return from his neck injury, but his season is over, according to Cubs insider Taylor McGregor .

Brown was trying to come back and provide some much-needed help for the Cubs pitching staff. He originally went on the injured list in June. However, after a bridge camp game in late August, he once again started experiencing symptoms of his neck injury.

That setback ultimately sealed his fate. Without Brown coming back, the Cubs will have to rely on the arms they have and potentially some other returning arms. Shelby Miller, Edward Cabrera, Javier Assad and Justin Steele could still come and save the Cubs' pitching staff.

The biggest issue for the Cubs has been the bullpen. The Cubs bullpen has a 4.02 ERA on the season, and in the second half, the bullpen has allowed 1.22 home runs per nine innings, ranked eighth-worst in baseball.

Brown was a swingman who could have started games if the Cubs needed him as well. He had a 1.85 ERA in 20 games this season. He had made eight starts and covered a total of 68 innings. He was having a great season, bouncing back from his 5.92 ERA last year.

The Cubs are suddenly in danger of falling out of the postseason entirely. They have lost 12 of their last 19 games and hold a 4 1/2 game lead in the wild card race. Winning the division seems extremely unlikely right now, as they sit nine games back of the Milwaukee Brewers. If they do not start playing better baseball soon, their lead in the wild card race will evaporate as the Arizona Diamondbacks and San Diego Padres close in.

articles.title: GB's Dart struggles with illness in second-round exit
articles.summary: Britain's Harriet Dart says she felt "under the weather" as she struggles in the heat during her second-round loss to Marie Bouzkova at the US Open.
articles.body:
Britain's Harriet Dart said she felt "under the weather" as she struggled in the heat during her second-round loss to Marie Bouzkova at the US Open.

Dart struggled for rhythm in a 6-2 6-2 defeat by Czech 25th seed Bouzkova as temperatures reached around 30C in New York.

Dart's defeat means Fran Jones is the last remaining Briton in either singles draw at Flushing Meadows.

Jones faces American 14th seed Iva Jovic later on Thursday.

Dart draped ice towels around her neck and used cold-air hoses at the changeovers against Bouzkova as she attempted to cool down.

"I have been a bit under the weather. It is what it is, sadly," Dart, 30, said.

"It was quite warm. I had a temperature, I was trying to cool down. I've played many weeks in a row.

"I am not used to air conditioning being pumped everywhere. We go from really hot outside to freezing inside.

"All credit to my opponent, she is an incredibly tough player, so even if I had been at full capacity, I don't know."

Dart, who is ranked 131st in the world, struggled on serve against Bouzkova, committing eight double faults and landing only 45% of her first serves.

Bouzkova took command almost straight away, winning seven games in a row to clinch the first set and go a double break up in the second.

From there Dart was unable to recover as Bouzkova safely saw out the rest of the match to reach the third round, where she will face Polish eighth seed Iga Swiatek.

Dart's exit follows compatriot Katie Boulter's second-round defeat by Karolina Muchova in only 58 minutes on Wednesday.

In the men's draw, Jacob Fearnley and Toby Samuel lost in the second round, while Cameron Norrie, Arthur Fery, Harry Wendelken and Jan Choinski exited in the first round.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka Snaps at Reporter During US Open Press Conference: ‘Think Before You Say Stuff’
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka takes her sport very seriously. After defeating Polina Iatcenko in the second round of the US Open in New York City on Wednesday, September 2...
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka takes her sport very seriously.

After defeating Polina Iatcenko in the second round of the US Open in New York City on Wednesday, September 2, the Belarusian tennis star, 28, was asked by a reporter about her "mood now that the tournament has started," in a press conference posted on YouTube .

"Obviously, last week it's lots of parties and fun and stuff like that," the reporter noted.

Sabalenka shook her head and interrupted, "You guys are, like, a joke. Parties, fun… like, why would ⁠you even say that? Why would ​you ⁠even think about that? Like, what kind of question is that?"

"Just because I posted, like, some activities with brands , and you think that I've been partying, not training?" the two-time US Open champ continued.

"I'm not saying you go to the parties and that you're…." the reporter tried to clarify.

"You literally said that," the No. 1 seed snapped, before adding, "Next question."

"For everyone who is unclear, I'm not suggesting that Aryna is having fun at these parties," the reporter continued.

"Thanks yeah," Sabalenka responded. "OK. Move on."

The reporter then tried to rephrase his question. "So now that the tournament has started, do you find you're getting quite serious and combative?"

"Oh, yeah, I wasn't serious before that. Next question," the clearly irritated athlete replied quickly.

As the next reporter began to speak, she blurted, "Think before you say stuff."

Sabalenka will face Kamilla Rakhimova in the third round on Friday, September 4.

articles.title: Michigan football schedule for 2027 gets update, including Texas game
articles.summary: College Football Week 0 will be eliminated and the entire FBS will open prior to Labor Day weekend. Here's the Michigan football 2027 schedule update.
articles.body:
Michigan football has tweaked its schedule for the 2027 season.

What has recently been known as "Week 0" has been eliminated and now the entire Football Bowl Subdivision will open its season prior to Labor Day weekend 2027.

As a result, Michigan's season opener against Buffalo has been moved to Aug. 28, its Week 2 matchup at Texas has been moved to Sept. 4 (previously Sept. 11) and the Wolverines will wrap up their nonconference season Sept. 11 against Eastern Michigan in Ann Arbor.

There was concern earlier this week after a report that U-M's game vs. EMU had been moved to the previously scheduled date with Texas, but a team spokesman told the Free Press it was simply the required schedule shuffling with the season being moved up and the big time matchup in Austin would be on as scheduled.

This also means Michigan will have two bye weeks in the 2027 season, though those dates (like the rest of the schedule) are still to be determined.

Michigan's return trip to Texas represents the back half of a home-and-home with the Longhorns . The first matchup came in 2024, when UT came to Ann Arbor and beat U-M 31-12 in Week 2.

This will mark the third time the two sides meet in the span of four seasons − the Longhorns beat the Wolverines 41-27 in the Cheez-It Citrus Bowl in Orlando, Fla. on Dec. 31, 2025, in a game coached by interim coach Biff Poggi, less than one week after Kyle Whittingham was named Michigan's new head man.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom files lawsuit against Sky following ejection, ban after altercation with Natasha Cloud
articles.summary: Enes Kanter Freedom has filed a federal complaint against the Chicago Sky and more after his ejection following an altercation with guard Natasha Cloud on Aug. 23.
articles.body: Enes Kanter Freedom is taking legal action against the Chicago Sky following his ejection from Wintrust Arena following an altercation with guard Natasha Cloud during a game against the Indiana Fever. Freedom filed his federal complaint in U.S. District Court, where he said he was "peacefully exercising my First Amendment rights" by sitting near the baseline and wearing a T-shirt that read, "WOMAN noun, adult human female." Freedom was banned indefinitely from Wintrust Arena by the Sky, and he said he may be pursuing legal action because of it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Freedom’s lawsuit names Chicago Women’s Basketball Operations, LLC, which operates the Sky, the Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority (MPEA), which financed and built Wintrust Arena as a public project, and the City of Chicago as defendants, claiming they "combined and conspired, and acted jointly to execute their conspiracy, to discriminate against Plaintiff based on Plaintiff’s verbal and demonstrable expression of viewpoint and gender identity when they wrongfully ejected Plaintiff from a recent WNBA game." "Defendants compounded and exacerbated Plaintiff’s injuries when they subsequently banned Plaintiff indefinitely from attendance," the lawsuit obtained by OutKick read. The lawsuit adds that Freedom "believes deeply and advocates forcefully that the integrity of women-only sports must be protected, and he has been explicit in many public appearances on this point." The suit also reiterates a point Freedom has made on numerous occasions, that he self-identifies as a player who is eligible to participate in the WNBA "because such declaration is all that is required by WNBA’s rules." Freedom has received backlash for his stance, which was also mentioned in the lawsuit. "Plaintiff has been the target of a torrent of hateful attacks and discriminatory actions based on Plaintiff’s viewpoint and gender identity," the lawsuit read. CHICAGO SKY OWNER OPENS UP ON ENES KANTER FREEDOM EJECTION, MAKES ANALOGY TO SHOOTING A GUN The lawsuit proceeds to break down the events on Aug. 23 in the eyes of Freedom, which began with his manager sending a "courteous text message" to Sky GM Jeff Pagliocca, his old personal trainer, to inform him the former NBA center would be attending the game. Pagliocca allegedly responded, "Appreciate the text," but Sky owner Michael Alter allegedly alerted Wintrust Arena Security of Freedom’s expected attendance. It continues by saying Freedom was harassed by Sky fans, many of whom used vulgar language including, "Get your b---- a—out of Chicago, f--- you b----, b---- a-- n-----!," among others. "None of these fans were warned or ejected, despite profanity and racial slurs being express violations of the WNBA Fan Code of Conduct," the lawsuit read. During the third quarter of the game, Freedom stood and raised his arms in celebration of a three-pointer made by Sophie Cunningham, the Fever star who has also received vitriol for her stance on biological men participating in women’s sports. A few possessions later, Cloud made a shot, and following a timeout, she "initiated a vulgar, profanity-laced verbal tired directed at Plaintiff Freedom personally, and charged nearly half the length of the court toward where Plaintiff Freedom was sitting courtside," the lawsuit read. "Plaintiff Freedom believes that Cloud’s attack was motivated and triggered by the message on Plaintiff’s shirt and Plaintiff’s widely publicized viewpoint on protecting the integrity of women only sports," the lawsuit added. The lawsuit states that, while Freedom raised his arms "in confusion and disbelief," Cloud continued to scream out profanities in his direction "in violation of WNBA rules." Cloud was not ejected from the game, nor did the WNBA issue any disciplinary action. Alter also confirmed the Sky would not take action against Cloud. The lawsuit adds that Alter "subsequently mischaracterized the interaction" between Freedom and Cloud, claiming the former was "chirping" at her before the altercation. It also mentioned an interview Alter had with OutKick, where he likened what Freedom did to shooting a gun at someone. "I mean, to use an extreme example, when you shoot a gun at someone, you don’t get a warning, ‘Don’t do that again.’ Your action doesn’t deserve a warning. You take action that becomes a threat, you don’t get a warning," Alter told OutKick. Freedom claimed that damages against him continue "as long as the unconstitutional ban" from Wintrust Arena stays in effect. Freedom requested the court declare the defendants violated his First Amendment rights by ejecting him from Wintrust Arena and indefinitely barring him from re-entry as well as"an award of nominal and compensatory damages for Plaintiff’s losses incurred." CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP "My T-shirt did what the whole [WNBA] apparently couldn’t: define a woman," Kanter’s X post with his lawsuit read. "No threats. No violence. Just biology. And somehow, that required a security escort. You don’t have to agree with my speech but you don’t get to silence me for it. I will not be intimidated. I will not be silenced. I will continue to stand for women and defend free speech." The Sky and MPEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment by OutKick regarding Kanter’s lawsuit. The City of Chicago doesn't comment on pending litigation, an official said.

articles.title: Super League: Bradford Bulls produce five-try first half to snap seven-match losing streak with win over Castleford Tigers
articles.summary: Bradford Bulls snapped a seven-match losing streak with a 32-22 win over Castleford Tigers; Sky Sports will show every Super League game live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live, while the remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+
articles.body:
Bulls had dropped to the bottom of the Betfred Super League table with a lengthy winless run which stretched back to July 10, but they were 18-0 up by the 19 minute mark after early scores for Riley Dean, Connor Wynne and Caleb Aekins.

Dan Russell and Waqa Blake added further tries before the break and whilst Tigers briefly railed, Ebon Scurr grabbed a sixth effort for the hosts after 52 minutes to keep alive Bulls' hopes of avoiding the wooden spoon ahead of next Thursday's season finale at 13th-placed York.

Bulls head coach Kurt Haggerty revealed this week his team had discussed the prospect of finishing bottom and it appeared to spark an instant response, with Dean able to run the ball in under the posts after five minutes.

Wynne dived over in the corner eight minutes later before Aekins finished off and even though Louis Senior got Tigers off the mark, Bulls ended the half with a bang when Chris Atkin sent over Russell for a 34th-minute score and Blake then beat the hooter.

It earned Bulls a healthy 26-4 half-time advantage which was quickly reduced when Krystian Mapapalangi successfully latched onto a grubber kick, but Scurr bundled over from close range to provide further delight for the home fans at Odsal Stadium.

Atkin kicked a fourth conversion before the Tigers claimed consolations through Alex Mellor and Mapapalangi, but Bulls would not be denied and eased to a first home victory in three months.

Bottom-of-the-table Bulls have drawn level on 14 points with York, Huddersfield Giants and Hull FC, but the trio are in action across this weekend before the regular Super League season concludes next week.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.summary: Teams in the AFC North can breathe easier in the 2026 NFL season, especially opposing quarterbacks of the Cleveland Browns, following the departure of Myles...
articles.body:
Teams in the AFC North can breathe easier in the 2026 NFL season, especially opposing quarterbacks of the Cleveland Browns, following the departure of Myles Garrett in the offseason .

Garrett is now in the NFC West after the Browns shockingly traded him to the Los Angeles Rams in June.

For years, Garrett terrorized opposing offenses in the AFC North, including the Pittsburgh Steelers. One player who surely has an ugly memory of Garrett in the division is Steelers backup quarterback Mason Rudolph .

Garrett once hit Rudolph in the head with a helmet during a game between the Browns and the Steelers in 2019, the former Oklahoma State Cowboys star signal-caller's first year in the NFL.

Steelers QB Happy That Myles Garrett is No Longer in the AFC North

During an appearance on Cam Heyward's Not Just Football podcast , the 31-year-old Rudolph was asked if he's glad that Garrett has been traded out of the division.

"As a Pittsburgh Steeler, I'm thrilled that he is no longer in the AFC North," Rudolph responded to Heyward's question.

"I think [coach] Mike McCarthy's fired up about that, I think [offensive coordinator] Brian Angelichio is fired up about that. I know our tackles are fired up about that. . . . And the top of my frontal lobe, yes."

During Garrett's time with Cleveland, he racked up 125.5 sacks in 134 games.

Still, there's a new pass rush star over in Cleveland that Rudolph and the Steelers have to be wary of. While Garrett is gone in the AFC North, the Browns got two-time Pro Bowl defensive end Jared Verse as part of the return from the Rams.

articles.title: Understanding Bill Guerin Helps The Devils Understand A Quinn Hughes Timeline
articles.summary: And whether the New Jersey Devils can sign Hughes next year, in 2030, or at all.
articles.body:
Minnesota Wild general manager Bill Guerin had a surprising interview on KFAN during the Minnesota State Fair. The interview, while providing plenty of cringeworthy moments, wasn't surprising. The fact that Guerin interviewed in the first place did.

Usually, GMs aren't public, especially during a big contract negotiation. Sure, Guerin wants to provide some transparency about the team ahead of a pivotal season, but he's been uncannily candid this summer. On the radio hit at the state fair, he admitted it was his third interview of the day.

The New Jersey Devils want an answer, or at least some clarity, on Quinn Hughes. Can they acquire him this season, in the offseason, or later? The saga weighed on the team last season, and it's no coincidence they fell apart after the star defenseman was traded from the Vancouver Canucks to the Minnesota Wild.

To understand the Hughes timeline, the Devils must understand Guerin, who is entering this offseason with a different perspective than he has in the past. The Wild have plenty of pressure heading into the season, yet Guerin seems confident that a deal will get done and the team will be in Stanley Cup contention.

While the Minnesota GM hasn't won a Stanley Cup and only one playoff series in his tenure, he's been on a heater. Guerin is on a roll that allows him to enter this season with more confidence, especially since his approach is working.

Guerin signed Kirill Kaprizov late last offseason, with the deal announced on Sept. 30. That was a tougher deal to negotiate because Kaprizov became the highest-paid player in the NHL despite playing the wing. That deal came down to the wire, but Guerin put it together.

He also made the Hughes trade in the first place, a bold move at the time that paid off. While Hughes couldn't choose his destination, he had a strong say in how he responded following his trade, and it was his best hockey since his Norris Trophy 2023-24 season. Guerin made the deal confident that the defenseman wanted to be there and buy in for a Wild team that's gone all in. And his play reflected his desire to stay in Minnesota, at least for the short term.

Guerin was the GM of the USA hockey team that won the Gold Medal at the Olympics. He took criticism for his team-building decisions, including leaving Jason Robertson, Lane Hutson, and Cole Caufield off the roster, but his strategy paid off. Plus, he won that Gold with both Jack and Quinn Hughes on the team, which is a bond that gives him more confidence in this round of negotiations.

Plus, Guerin won the Jim Gregory Award as the GM of the year. The award reflects the respect he has around the league. Add it all up, and he enters this season more confident than ever before.

It's well documented that Quinn wants to play with his brothers. With Jack and Luke on the Devils, they have the edge, but it's not a given that he'll join them right away. There's a good chance he teams up with his brothers, specifically Jack, in the 2030 offseason, in Minnesota, New Jersey, or anywhere else.

Guerin wants to meet Hughes halfway. He wants to win, and Guerin can make the argument that the Wild are in a better position to do so, both this season and the next three. Hughes wants to play with his brothers, and he can do so with a deal that aligns with Jack. The Cale Makar $20.5 million average annual value contract is a reference, and both sides will meet somewhere close to the record-breaking deal while still having enough cap space to add talent to an already contending team.

Even if Hughes refuses to sign, a message that he's leaving at the end of the season, there's a good chance Guerin keeps him and doesn't trade him. Guerin is one of the most aggressive GMs in the NHL, and his track record suggests he'll go all in, knowing this season is his best chance to win the Cup.

It's easy to say that the Devils must ignore the noise and plan for a season without Hughes. It's easier said than done, especially since they tried last season. The reality is that the Devils must remain patient, even for a new GM in Sunny Mehta, who has kicked off the ground running with a surplus of moves.

The Devils, Mehta specifically, must plan for an extension. He must keep that possibility open. If the Wild extend Hughes to a three-year deal, the contest for the Devils is to have a better outlook in a few seasons to win a Cup than the Wild, or any team that makes sense for the star defenseman.

A short-term deal also might not be the worst thing for the Devils either. If the Hughes deal happens with the Wild, the Devils will have more resources to upgrade their roster and make it more appealing to him in a few years.

When Mehta took over, he kept the door open to make a splash. Presumably, it was to land Hughes. However, an extension would let him use the depth he built recently to acquire a player like Connor Hellebuyck or Dylan Larkin. It's unlikely, but something the Mehta must be prepared to do, especially if he's looking to convince Hughes that the Devils are in the best spot to contend in both the short and long term.

articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs received brutal Ben Brown news before Thursday night's game against the Milwaukee Brewers. The post Chicago Cubs Receive Brutal Ben Brown Ne...
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs are set to play the Milwaukee Brewers in the series finale of a four-game set at Wrigley Field at 6:15 p.m. CDT on Thursday.

The Cubs won the first game of the series 17-3 on Monday. The Brewers won 9-4 on Tuesday and 9-5 on Wednesday.

Ahead of Thursday's game, the Cubs received brutal news involving injured right-hander Ben Brown.

Chicago Cubs Get Rough Ben Brown News During Brewers Series

Brown, who has been on the IL since late June due to a neck injury, will miss the remainder of the season.

Via Marquee Sports' Taylor McGregor on X : Ben Brown will be out the remainder of the season with the neck injury.

Brown appeared on the verge of returning from the IL late last month. Unfortunately, Brown became symptomatic in a bullpen session roughly a week ago, and it worsened as the day progressed, according to Meghan Montermurro of the Chicago Tribune .

Losing Brown for the rest of the season is a major blow for the Cubs, who currently own the second National League Wild Card spot.

articles.title: HyVee Team of the Week: Mill Valley girls flag football
articles.summary: The Mill Valley High School girls flag football team is your FOX4 HyVee Team of the Week.
articles.body:
OVERLAND PARK, Kan. -- The Mill Valley High School girls flag football team is your FOX4 HyVee Team of the Week.

Winning a championship is never easy. Winning back-to-back titles is even harder. The Lady Jaguars are looking to accomplish that this year after capping off a 13-1 season just a year ago.

Although, this season looks a little different. Girls flag football is officially sanctioned as a varsity high school sport in Kansas. With the inaugural season underway, the Jaguars are looking to hit the ground running.

"We're really excited for this year," Kate Mikuls, Mill Valley QB and senior said. "Obviously like new competition, so it's going to be a lot different, but I think we're ready and we're expecting to be challenged this year, we're expecting to have a little bit of a chip on our shoulder and we're hoping that we can defend out title."

Just like any high school sport, there's new players on the squad each year. Last year's team had 28 girls on the roster, 12 of those players came back this year. With a lot of new faces on the team, many of which who have never played football, senior Paige Frost says watching them grow has been an awarding experience."

"Watching them grow is a really fun exciting thing, so just being that bigger mentor to them is just huge to me," Frost said.

Already knowing what it feels like to win a championship, Frost and the other returning players are looking to do it again.

As the team participates in a sport that continues to grow, Head Coach Carter Sebasto says winning team of the week is proof that hard work pays off.

"Grateful for them to be rewarded with something like this because they've been putting in the work, dealing with the heat, we've been up every morning 5 a.m. getting started so they deserve something like this."

articles.title: Brendan Gallagher Reveals Major 1st Impressions Of Canucks
articles.summary: As part of the moves made by the Vancouver Canucks during the offseason, they acquired forward Brendan Gallagher from the Montréal Canadiens in exchange for...
articles.body:
As part of the moves made by the Vancouver Canucks during the offseason, they acquired forward Brendan Gallagher from the Montréal Canadiens in exchange for future considerations.

Gallagher, a 14-year NHL veteran who had played his entire career with the Canadiens up until this summer, joins a Canucks group who finished dead-last in the Western Conference standings last season.

Even though his offensive production dipped in his final campaign with Montreal, he's hoping to use his veteran status to help bring along the younger players in the Canucks organization looking to get their feet wet at the NHL level.

Brendan Gallagher Is Looking Forward To A "Fun" New Chapter With The Vancouver Canucks

For Gallagher, it's the first time in his NHL career that he's been traded, but he's handling it as best he can, and so far, it's been a productive endeavor meeting his new teammates and skating with them informally.

"It's the first time I've had to go through this as a pro, and it's different. So, you want to spend as much time in your new environment as possible, get to know your teammates, and it's been really productive, and I'm enjoying it," Gallagher said via NHL.com.

"It's a really good group. You can tell the guys get along right away, and you know it's going to be fun," Gallagher said. "Everyone's excited to be here, everyone's excited to get back to work, and these are fun times for us."

Meanwhile, Gallagher and his wife recently welcomed a second child.

"It's been awesome. My wife is handling a lot right now, so obviously very appreciative to have her. Having two under two is just as tough as they always say, and she's taking the brunt of it right now," Gallagher said. "We're very happy, and there's nothing like becoming a parent, and it feels just as amazing the second time as well."

Brendan Gallagher Played The First 14 Years Of His NHL Career With The Canadiens

Gallagher, who was taken by the Canadiens with the 147th overall pick in the 2010 NHL Draft, has skated in 911 career games in a Montreal jersey, and has tallied 246 goals with 241 assists for 487 points.

He's also contributed 14 goals with 20 assists in 79 career Stanley Cup Playoff games.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton's breakup with the Brewers becomes official at Wrigley
articles.summary: The Wisconsin native's split from his hometown team traces back to a canceled invite after the Packers knocked out the Bucks in 2024. He hasn't forgotten.
articles.body:
Tyrese Haliburton spent the past two years dumping his hometown baseball team in public, one jersey at a time. On Thursday night, he made it official at Wrigley Field.

The injured Indiana Pacers point guard threw out the ceremonial first pitch wearing a Cubs jersey before Chicago hosted the Brewers , taking the mound at Wrigley rather than 90 miles north in Milwaukee.

Haliburton, from Oshkosh, Wisconsin, was a Brewers fan his whole life. That ended in 2024, he said , when the team invited him to throw out a first pitch that summer, then pulled the offer after his Pacers eliminated the Milwaukee Bucks in the playoffs.

"I was a Brewers fan and then I was supposed to throw the first pitch last summer and then they X'd that after the playoffs ended," Haliburton said on the "The Pat McAfee Show" in April 2025 . "So I said, you know what, I'm no longer a Brewers fan."

It was a rough break up. Haliburton started showing up to Pacers games in Cubs and Dodgers gear, including a Cubs jersey at a preseason game in October 2025. When the Dodgers swept the Brewers out of the National League Championship Series that fall, he leaned into rooting against Milwaukee.

The Dodgers noticed. Manager Dave Roberts invited Haliburton to jump on the bandwagon and throw out a first pitch at Dodger Stadium.

"I'd like to offer him the first pitch at Dodger Stadium, and he can rock that Ohtani jersey in its rightful place," Roberts said on Amazon's "Good Sports With Kevin Hart and Kenan Thompson."

Haliburton, who calls himself a baseball free agent, has had plenty of time to practice his first pitch. He tore his Achilles tendon in Game 7 of the NBA Finals against Oklahoma City Thunder in June 2025 and was out for the entire 2025-26 season. The Pacers have said he isn't expected to play again until late 2026.

articles.title: Army football QB Cale Hellums made offseason strides
articles.summary: Army senior quarterback Cale Hellums is confident he has made strides since last season.
articles.body:
PHOTOS: Army football 2026 preseason scrimmages

Army football offensive coordinator Cody Worley was talking to head coach Jeff Monken this week about the developmental similarities of recent quarterback Bryson Daily and current starter Cale Hellums.

Both signal callers had to wait patiently for two years to get their opportunity to assume the QB1 position for the Black Knights . Both saw success and difficulty in their junior seasons, leading Army to six regular-season wins. And both made great strides in understanding and patience headed into their senior season – at least that's what Worley believes about Hellums, another Texan who's going to lead the Army offense when the 2026 season opens on Saturday, Sept. 5, against Bryant .

Speaking of Hellums' development, Worley said, "Just the comfort with the system, the comfort with the speed of the game with what we're asking him to do and how we're asking him to do it – I would say it's on par with the improvements that Bryson made from junior to senior year.''

Daily was the heir apparent for the 2023 season.

"Junior year, Bryson Daily turned the ball over 11 times, and he looked like a guy that wasn't comfortable yet,'' Worley said.

A year later, in 2024, Daily guided Army to 11 of its 12 wins and finished just outside of the top five in Heisman Trophy voting.

Fast forward to 2025, and Hellums worked his way up from third string to stepping in for injured starter Dewayne Coleman in the second game at Kansas State , where he set a program record with 41 carries, and his third touchdown with under three minutes to play capped a 24-21 upset win.

The high of victory for Hellums was smashed with three early turnovers and subsequent yank from the lineup the following week against North Texas, and Coleman regained his starting role for the following two weeks. Hellums, who saw duty in all 13 games, was back as starter in game six against Charlotte and did not relinquish the job the rest of the way.

"I think the best teacher is learning (first-hand) and learning from your mistakes, and that's how you become better,'' Hellums said of his junior-year experience at the helm.

Hellums had a lot to be proud of, averaging over 23 carries per game, gaining 1,223 yards and scoring 18 touchdowns. He also threw for four scores and 694 yards while operating the run-heavy offense, throwing just three interceptions.

Since last season, Monken kept open the battle for starting quarterback with sophomores Bryson Luter and Ethan Washington, but it was understood the job was Hellums' to lose.

"Cale Hellums has made a drastic improvement, and I'll say drastic,'' Worley said. "The game has finally slowed down for him, and he's able to execute at a high level. He's been really consistent with decision making, much improved in fundamentals and option (offense) framework and understanding what we're trying to do. And with that, it's allowed him to be a voice and a leader as well.''

Said Hellums, "I think just having that year under my belt and then coming into the offseason with the guys and continue to perform and get better, I'm hoping that I (improved) on the right skills, and I'm ready to showcase it when the season starts.'

"I'm not perfect, and I'm not where I want to be at overall – there's always things I can improve on and be a better football player, a better teammate and a better leader. I guess in a couple days we're going to find out if I've gotten better … I hope I have. I think I have, but we'll find out one way or another.''

Hellums said it was always his childhood dream to play quarterback at the Division I level and eventually become the starter.

"By the grace of God, I've been able to fulfill that,'' he said. "God has blessed me day in and day out, and to put me here, to be able to lead this team is the greatest blessing that one could ask for. … It's very humbling. … I'm just forever grateful for this opportunity.''

articles.title: Katie Taylor aims to repay fans for 'support over the years' in Croke Park finale
articles.summary: Ireland's Katie Taylor aims for a fairytale finish to an extraordinary boxing story as she drops the curtain on her career at Dublin's Croke Park.
articles.body:
Sept 3 (Reuters) - Ireland's Katie Taylor will bring down the curtain on her career with a fight against Flora Pili ​of France at Dublin's Croke Park on Saturday in which she will try to achieve a fairytale finish to ‌an extraordinary boxing story.

Taylor, 40, has come a long way from covering her hair and pretending to be a boy to get fights in the junior ranks, and the showdown in front of thousands of fanatical Irish fans is her chance to bow out as the undisputed super-lightweight champion of the world.

"I'm ​not sure if there's any other country in the world where 80,000 people would turn up for a female athlete," ​Taylor told reporters in Dublin.

"I'm so grateful for the support. I'm blown away by it, to be honest. ⁠I want to put on a performance worthy of everyone's support over the years. This country has traveled around the world to ​watch me fight … and they'll be with me again on Saturday night."

Of Ireland's 42 Olympic medals, 19 have come in the boxing ring, ​and Taylor's gold at the 2012 Olympics was a defining moment for the women's sport. Four years later she turned pro, amassing titles and professional purses that she could only have dreamed of when starting out.

A native of the seaside town of Bray, just south of Dublin, Taylor tore through the professional ranks, ​using her speed and aggression to win the WBA title in her seventh professional fight, and she has barely looked back since.

Together ​with Amanda Serrano, she became the first woman to headline a card at New York's Madison Square Garden when they fought in April 2022, with Taylor ‌winning ⁠a fight for the ages in a razor-thin split decision.

It has, however, not all been plain sailing. A gangland shooting at the Regency Hotel near Croke Park, in which one man was killed at a 2016 weigh-in, brought professional boxing in Ireland to a standstill.

Katie Taylor: 'This is what it's all about'

When she finally got to fight in the Irish capital in May 2023, Taylor suffered the only defeat of her professional career as Chantelle Cameron ​edged her on the judges' ​scorecards. And though she won ⁠a rematch at the same venue six months later, the original loss still stung.

Now, though, she has the chance to go out in a blaze of glory. The 29-year-old Pili will provide a tough test, ​but Taylor's focus is solely on getting her hand raised one last time.

Taylor performed an open ​workout on Wednesday ⁠at a venue on the north side of Dublin, picking out a young girl from the crowd to share the ring with her, and 10-year-old Clodagh Keating burst into tears as her idol laced up a pair of boxing gloves for her.

"To feel the atmosphere even in this small ⁠arena, I ​can't imagine what Saturday night's going to be like, and getting the chance ​to meet little Clodagh there, who got into the ring, this is what it's all about for me," Taylor said.

"In a few days, I'll make my last ring walk ​and I'll look back on this in a few years, and I imagine I'll be overwhelmed."

articles.title: Raiders Hit With Blunt Warning Regarding WR Corps
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders could have a serious problem at the wide receiver position heading into the 2026 regular season. The post Raiders Hit With Blunt Warnin...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders offense has some potential this season, but the passing offense could struggle. The wide receiver room is still a pretty big concern.

The Raiders' wide receiver room was a mess last season, but they didn't do much to upgrade it this offseason. The team might have the best tight end duo in the NFL with Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer, but it would help to have players who can get open on the outside.

Las Vegas is headed in the right direction. There's a lot to like from what they did this offseason. However, the lack of wide receiver talent could really derail the offense. CBS Sports' Jordan Dajani put together a list of one reason each team in the AFC could disappoint this season. He listed wide receiver as the biggest reason for the Raiders.

"The Las Vegas Raiders had probably the worst wide receiver room in the NFL last year with Tre Tucker and Jack Bech," Dajani wrote. "To bolster the unit, Vegas added former Minnesota Vikings WR3 Jalen Nailor and drafted Malik Benson in the sixth round.

"Tight end Brock Bowers is going to be the star of this passing attack, but Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza don't appear to have any big playmakers out wide."

It's hard to feel too excited about anybody in the Raiders' wide receiver room. There isn't one clear breakout candidate.

Tre Tucker is a good player, but might be a No. 3 receiver on most NFL teams. Jack Bech is a former second-round pick, but he hasn't shown enough to believe he can be an impact player. The Athletic's Mike Sando polled executives around the league to rank the teams in the AFC. The Raiders came in at No. 12, and a big reason for the low rating was the wide receiver room.

"(Klint) Kubiak maximized Sam Darnold and found a way to feed JSN (Jaxon Smith-Njigba) in Seattle, and his offense started out hot in Derek Carr's final year with New Orleans," an exec told The Athletic. "But Kirk is immobile, (Ashton) Jeanty is starting off injured and it's such a top-heavy offensive roster. It is Jeanty, (Brock) Bowers and then probably the worst receiver room in the league along with Miami."

Tucker had a career-high 696 receiving yards last season, and he was the No. 1 option after Jakobi Meyers got traded. He's clearly a good player, but being a No. 1 wide receiver in Week 1 is a different beast.

Tucker is really fast, but his hands have been an issue in the past, and he's a bit undersized at 5-foot-8. One executive is buying that having Tucker as a No. 1 wide receiver is a recipe for success.

"If you are scheming up stuff for Tre Tucker as your 1, yikes," the exec told The Athletic. "I like Jalen Nailor as an add, but what was he, a third at best in Minnesota? Kubiak is definitely going to have his offensive guru-ness tested."

articles.title: HS Standouts: Clinton Red Devils’ Owen Glenn and Angelo Cromer
articles.summary: When Clinton High School varsity football needed one final drive against its biggest area rival, the Red Devils turned to a lethal quarterback and running ba...
articles.body:
CLINTON, S.C. (WSPA) - When Clinton High School varsity football needed one final drive against its biggest area rival, the Red Devils turned to a lethal quarterback and running back duo.

Senior QB Owen Glenn and senior RB Angelo Cromer helped spearhead Clinton's dramatic 29-22 victory over Laurens on Aug. 28, extending the Red Devils' winning streak over their arch-rival to six straight games. Laurens and Clinton have played over 107 times.

With the game tied late in the fourth quarter, Glenn led Clinton on a 10-play, 75-yard game-winning drive. The march ended with a 3-yard touchdown pass with just two seconds remaining, sending the Red Devils into celebration mode and handing Laurens another heartbreaking defeat.

For Glenn, the key was staying composed when the game hung in the balance.

"I just know there was two minutes left in the game." said Glenn. "We're still tied, and I didn't really want to lose. I hate losing. So, I just tried to stay calm as much as I could and finish the game. It was a great experience, really emotional, but it was a fun game being that close."

The moment quickly became one of the highlights of Glenn's athletic career, which has already featured success in multiple sports.

The 6-foot-1, 175-pound senior is one of Clinton's most versatile athletes. In addition to leading the football program, Glenn plays varsity basketball as a forward and center and helped the Red Devils capture the AA State Baseball Championship this past spring. Balancing three varsity sports leaves little downtime, but Glenn embraces the challenge.

Playing his senior season at Clinton carries extra significance because of his family's deep roots in the community.

"I've been waiting to play here my whole life. I've been really looking forward to it. It's crazy that it's already here, but I'm really excited for the season," said Glenn.

The rivalry win was special not only because of what was at stake, but because many of the players on both sidelines have known each other for years.

"A lot of us are really close." said Glenn. A lot of the people that played for Laurens played with us when we were younger in baseball and football."

Standing alongside Glenn every step of the way has been Cromer, one of the area's most explosive running backs.

The 5-foot-10, 170-pound senior rushed 17 times for 152 yards against Laurens, averaging nearly nine yards per carry while consistently creating chunk plays for Clinton's offense. His performance added to an impressive varsity career that now includes 1,159 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns.

Football has been part of Cromer's life since he was young, and he still remembers exactly when his love for the sport began when he took his first hit.

"I started playing football when I was several, three. I feel like my first year, I just fell in love with the game." said Cromer.

Cromer's passion has translated into a relentless work ethic. Behind Clinton High School sits a hill that has become a training ground for the senior running back.

"We got a big old hill outside our school and I run about ten rounds a day," said Cromer.

For Cromer, the workouts are about mental toughness as much as physical preparation.

"It teaches you to keep going and don't give up," said Cromer. "It's a big hill. Sometimes I don't have water. Sometimes I get dirty. It just keeps me going."

When Glenn connected on the game-winning touchdown pass against Laurens, Cromer had the same reaction as much of the Clinton fan base.

Although he's become one of Clinton's most productive offensive weapons, Cromer is quick to credit those around him for his development.

"I'm blessed to have the teammates that I have," said Cromer. "If it wasn't for them, I wouldn't be where I am today."

The partnership between Glenn and Cromer stretches back far beyond varsity football. Their years together have helped build the chemistry that showed throughout the season opener.

Now entering the final chapter of their high school careers, both seniors are thinking about what comes next after graduation.

Cromer hopes to serve in the United States Army, following a path inspired by members of his family who have served before him. Meanwhile, Glenn wants to play football in college, but if that doesn't work out he's considered becoming a Navy SEAL if he chooses to pursue military service after high school, giving the longtime teammates another shared goal beyond athletics.

"I want to go to the military. I want to be in the Army." said Cromer

Whether their futures take them onto a football field, into military service, or somewhere else entirely, both athletes are focused on making the most of their final season in a Clinton uniform.

articles.title: Is Hearts' McPake poised to gatecrash Pocognoli's Scotland squad?
articles.summary: Josh McPake has made a significant impact since joining Hearts. Could he now do the same for the Scotland national team?
articles.body:
On the eve of the Scottish FA's highly-anticipated summit on youth development in Scotland, one of the country's own stole the show in a thrilling Edinburgh derby.

And as it happened, the new national team head coach, Sebastien Pocognoli, was in the Easter Road stands as Josh McPake spearheaded Hearts' entertaining victory over Hibernian.

Even before the Belgian was appointed, there were some calls from the Tartan Army to include the 25-year-old winger, such has been his emphatic start to life in Gorgie since making the switch from St Johnstone in the summer.

The clamour for his inclusion is now becoming inescapable.

A Rangers youth product, the question hanging over McPake since signing his pre-contract with Hearts in January, was could he cut it among the big boys.

Under the lights in Leith, McPake waltzed through the weak Hibs backline before bending a beautiful effort beyond Raphael Sallinger - with a deflection off Grant Hanley - sparking bedlam among the travelling supporters behind the goal.

The talk of the toon are the boys in maroon, but the chat in all corners of the country is about McPake. He really is the man of the moment.

In eight games, he has registered two goals and four assists for an increasingly easy-on-the-eye Hearts side, who are emerging as contenders for the campaign's great entertainers.

In the first 30 minutes at the home of their city rivals, they were magnificent. McPake - along with fellow Scotland hopeful Calvin Miller - was unplayable, hugging the touchline and leaving home full-back Felix Passlack for dust.

He destroyed the former Borussia Dortmund defender before teeing up James Wilson's opener, with former Hearts striker Ryan Stevenson explaining that was the perfect example of how much of a handful he is.

"It is so hard for defenders when wingers play on the opposite side," Stevenson said on Sportsound. "They always want to come on the inside, but he is happy to go on the outside and feint and go on his left side.

"One of his biggest attributes is you don't know which way he will go."

That was evident again when McPake took a stroll for his superb solo goal, one he was desperate for in his first derby.

"I thought we started the game really, really well," McPake told BBC Sport Scotland. "Obviously, I got the assist in the first half, but I really, really wanted the goal."

While he was happy to admit his desire to get on the scoresheet, the winger was a little more reluctant to indulge in any Scotland call-up conversation.

As understandable and mature as that may be, it won't stop the rest of us doing so. But McPake is more reserved than most because of his tricky route to the top.

After coming through the Rangers ranks, he was sent out on loan six times, before finally settling at Stirling Albion in League 1.

Impressing, he caught the eye of St Johnstone, albeit he was initially involved in their top-flight relegation.

It was in the second-tier last term where McPake started to shine. Head and shoulders above the rest, Derek McInnes' Hearts secured his services on a pre-contract. Then McInnes left Tynecastle for Ibrox.

"These things happen in football," explained McPake, who couldn't hide his appreciation for Vrancken.

That feeling is reciprocated. Even if the attacker was left out of Hearts initial European squad.

"It was a difficult start and he had to adapt in several ways and the things we wanted to see and be decisive in certain moments," the head coach said.

"But he did great and picked up those things and he is really strong in defence as well as offence and I'm pleased to see this happening."

And it appears Vrancken isn't the only one, with the winger dominating much of the post-match discussions.

"I know he has had loan moves, but it is about getting the right environment and the right manager," former Hibs midfielder Scott Allan said on Sportsound.

"Now he has landed with Wouter Vrancken and I think he will be a manager who will enhance his career.

"When they get him isolated, he puts defenders under pressure.

"I wouldn't be surprised if he is named in the next Scotland squad because he is the standout at present."

While McPake might be the standout, he has a more than decent support act.

Fellow forwards Miller and Wilson are in the mix for involvement in the upcoming Nations League games this month, too.

Teenager Wilson has already been capped, but since spending the second half of last season on loan with Tottenham Hotspur's under-21 side, he has taken his game up a notch.

His second derby goal at Easter Road will have done his hopes of a national team return no harm - nor will his wonderstrike against Rapid Vienna - with Stevenson adding he showed "total striker's instinct".

"We have to come to the point with a new manager coming in for Scotland, there is room to bring in a bit of freshness," he added.

Not dominating the discourse as much as last week for his heroics in Austria, hirpling into the box to score in extra-time and force penalties before netting his own, Miller strengthened his case yet again for an impressive performance.

He was spoken off in some circles as an outside shout for a World Cup spot following his superb Falkirk form, but that always seemed too much of a stretch.

But now, he and his team-mates are front and centre, catching the eye of everyone watching. Mr Pocognoli, are you watching?
authors: Amy Canavan - BBC Sport Scotland at Easter Road
