articles.title: Victor Robles placed on family medical emergency list, Stuart Fairchild recalled, Brennen Davis to the IL
articles.summary: A couple difficult moves for Seattle’s depth.
articles.body:
The Seattle Mariners announced Thursday that they've placed OF Victor Robles on the family medical emergency/bereavement list. Robles is allowed up to three days on the list, and though the exact nature of the situation is unknown, kindness and best wishes are being sent his and his family's way. Robles is currently in the Dominican Republic with his family, which is where Mariners GM Justin Hollander said he "needs to be."

In his stead, Seattle has recalled OF Stuart Fairchild, the local product who Seattle acquired midway through this season. As of pregame Thursday, Fairchild isn't yet with the club, needing to travel from where Tacoma is playing in Albuquerque. Additionally, Seattle recalled OF Brennen Davis from Triple-A Tacoma and placed him on the 60-day injured list, immediately removing him from the 40-man roster. Davis had been dealing this season with a severe hamstring strain that's kept him out all year; most recently, he suffered an oblique injury while swinging in the cages, and has now had a setback with that oblique that will end his season.

Occupying a bench and defensive replacement role when healthy this year for the most part, Robles will be mostly a 1-1 swap for Fairchild in the next few days. Though not quite the base stealer Robles is, Fairchild roams the outfield well and runs enough to fill in. The Seattle Prep product has been a stellar hitter in Triple-A this year in his age 30 campaign, and has played in parts of the last six seasons in the bigs.

Davis is a bittersweet move, as the 26 year old outfielder who spent years near the top of prospect lists spent much of this season on the sidelines once again, unable to ring the bell when Seattle was scouring its system for any sort of offensive spark. By adding him to the 40-man roster earlier this year, Seattle retained Davis following a scorching hot spring and excellent season with the Tacoma Rainiers. Unfortunately, as has been the case every year of his career, his body betrayed him, first with the hamstring, and then the oblique. By putting him on the IL, Davis will be paid for the remainder of the year at a big league minimum rate, a goodwill gesture from Seattle for a player who by all accounts is a diligent, hard worker and high-quality teammate. Seattle may also choose to retain Davis through the winter on their 40-man roster without needing to expose him to minor league free agency once again, though it's unclear if they'd choose to do so.

articles.title: Adley Rutschman returns to Camden Yards — and homers in the 1st inning for the Red Sox
articles.summary: Adley Rutschman homered in his first at-bat in his return to Camden Yards, hitting a drive to right field for the Boston Red Sox in the top of the first inni...
articles.body:
BALTIMORE (AP) — Adley Rutschman homered in his first at-bat in his return to Camden Yards, hitting a drive to right field for the Boston Red Sox in the top of the first inning at Baltimore on Thursday night.

Rutschman received a standing ovation from the crowd — and from the Baltimore dugout — when he came to the plate with two outs in the first. Then he slugged a 1-1 pitch from Brandon Young over the wall in right field. It was his 10th homer of the season and second since being traded from the Orioles to the Red Sox in early August.

Rutschman also received a video tribute between the first and second innings, and he got another big ovation despite having already done some damage offensively for his new team.

"A lot of memories, a lot of positive experiences. The people in Baltimore have always treated me with an unbelievable amount of respect and love, and I've always felt that when I've been here," Rutschman said before the game. "So just a huge thank you from the bottom of my heart."

Rutschman has battled elbow issues of late, but he was back in the lineup after missing the previous three games.

"It's a lot of feelings going on. Different being over on this side," he said. "A lot of memories, a lot of positive memories."

Baltimore drafted Rutschman No. 1 overall in 2019. His arrival in the major leagues in 2022 was part of a significant turnaround in which the Orioles ultimately won the AL East in 2023 and made the playoffs in 2024.

However, the last two years have been a good deal less successful. Although Rutschman made the All-Star team for the third time this year, the Orioles traded him to Boston just before the deadline.

"It's nothing but positive things to say about the Orioles, the organization, the staff, the players, coaches, just from top to bottom," Rutschman said. "From getting drafted up until the trade deadline this year, it's been a phenomenal experience."

Rutschman is now in better position to make the playoffs. Boston is almost certain to qualify, currently holding the second wild card. The Orioles have managed to stay in the race without him. They entered Thursday night one game behind Cleveland for the third wild card.

So there was a decent amount at stake once the pregame reunions were over.

"He couldn't help himself. He stopped into the clubhouse quickly," Orioles manager Craig Albernaz said. "A lot of hugs, a lot of crap talk going back and forth. It was good to see him."

articles.title: Our 2026 Journey Begins
articles.summary: Notre Dame opens its highly anticipated 2026 season on Sunday night on the hallowed ground of Lambeau Field. The Fighting Irish take on the Wisconsin Badgers...
articles.body:
Notre Dame opens its highly anticipated 2026 season on Sunday night on the hallowed ground of Lambeau Field. The Fighting Irish take on the Wisconsin Badgers in a Shamrock Series game originally scheduled in 2020. COVID interrupted those plans after Notre Dame had beaten the Badgers in 2019 at Soldier Field in Chicago. The subsequent changes within these programs and throughout all of college football were unimaginable back then. That aside, each team needs to make a statement in this game. NBC and Peacock will provide national television coverage from Green Bay starting at 7:30 PM Eastern Time.

Irish head coach Marcus Freeman and Wisconsin's Luke Fickell were working together at Cincinnati six short years ago. Freeman was the Defensive Coordinator (DC) under Fickell until leaving for South Bend in January 2021. After one season as Notre Dame's DC, Freeman ascended to the top job when Brian Kelly cut and ran. One year later, Fickell departed Cincinnati to take over in Madison. Their respective fortunes have diverged significantly since then. Freeman is 43-12 and beloved at Notre Dame while Fickell is a disappointing 17-21 for the Badgers. His seat is widely characterized in the media as very warm.

Several factors have plagued the Badgers in the Fickell era. One criticism is that the program had lost its identity as a power running machine. A more obvious issue is that Wisconsin was late to the party regarding the advent of NIL. They also did not warmly embrace the transfer portal as a roster building tool. Badger faithful need only consider the path of fellow Big-10 mediocrity Indiana when evaluating their own struggles. The Hoosiers turned themselves into a national powerhouse through their aggressive portal and NIL strategy. They also hired a head coach who pushed them in that direction. Badger fans wonder if something similar could happen in Wisconsin.

Fickell responded to this question during the offseason. He orchestrated a complete program reset in schemes, training methods, and personnel evaluation. The Badgers brought in 27 transfers. As many as 12 are expected to earn starting roles. This includes quarterback Colton Joseph, tailback Abu Sama, and four of five members of the secondary. It will be interesting to see how these players mesh over the course of the year. Unfortunately for Fickell, this matchup against a loaded Irish squad is no way to ease into the season.

Despite the challenges his team faces, Badger coach was philosophical about his 2026 team. "We have a lot of unknowns", he said. "I think that's the beauty of it, right? I mean, we got a new quarterback that we feel really good about. I'm sure you'll ask questions about him. But we also have never seen him truly play a game and look in the eyes of those things. And so that's what I think us as coaches, what continues to drive us and motivate us, but also keep us up at night. And so excited about getting to the 6th, that's for sure."

Meanwhile, Freeman and Notre Dame are still haunted by their own failures last September. They have reevaluated their offseason preparation regimen and made unspecified changes. A significant advantage for the Irish is they return so many experienced players, led by quarterback CJ Carr. The fact that Freeman's Coordinators are back also helps immensely. No one needs to learn new schemes or terminology. In short, Notre Dame should hit the ground running. Freeman knows there will be no acceptable excuses if they do not.

On the injury front, the Irish lost guard Matty Augustine to a broken foot last month. He is expected to return in late October. Fellow guard Charles Jagusah remains out indefinitely with a broken humerus after missing the 2025 season. Wideout Quincy Porter is also sidelined with a knee issue that has been slow to heal. Linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa, who is recovering from last season's ACL tear, is listed as questionable. Finally, it should be noted that Adon Shuler lost his father earlier this week. This was an unexpected tragedy and it is not yet known whether Shuler will elect to play on Sunday.

The Badgers also have a few injury concerns. Starting offensive linemen Emerson Mandell and Kevin Heywood have practiced sparingly in the past few weeks. Fickell said he will not know until Sunday if they will play. Both seem unlikely to start based on various insider reports.

NOTRE DAME'S OFFENSE vs. WISCONSIN'S DEFENSE

Offensive Coordinator Mike Denbrock is in a good place regarding his starting quarterback. Most of his skill position players, however, are question marks. At tailback, junior Aneyas Williams is the only known commodity. He can run, catch, and is a willing blocker. Behind Williams is Kedren Young, who returns to the field after missing the 2025 season due to knee surgery. Untested sophomore Nolan James is next, followed by two talented freshmen. Javian Osborne is better known of the two because Jonaz Walton missed spring practice with a wrist injury. What happens when Williams needs a breather is anyone's guess. There is plenty of talent within this group but as yet it is unproven.

Wide receiver is another area that is shrouded in mystery. Jordan Faison is a known, valuable commodity and is clearly Carr's favorite target. Jaden Greathouse is back after an injury plagued 2025. Can he or anyone else become an elite receiver this season? Transfer Mylan Graham from Ohio State has all the necessary physical gifts. Will they translate into production? Junior Micah Gilbert has earned the job as the starter at field receiver. He has flashed impressive skills in the past but can he become a consistent and reliable target?

Others in the rotation include lacrosse star Matt Jeffery, Elijah Burress, Cam Williams, Logan Saldate, and Jerome Bettis. Freshman Bubba Frazier has impressed the coaches with elite speed and quickness. He could see action at the slot receiver position. Will any of these players separate from the pact to solidify the passing attack?

Veteran tight end Cooper Flanagan is healthy after missing virtually all of 2025 while recovering from an Achilles tear. He and backup James Flanigan are valued more for their blocking ability rather than as receivers. Role players Ty Washington and Jack Larsen round out the rotation. Can any of these players deliver clutch third down and red zone receptions? Many Irish observers believe the future belongs to freshman sensation Ian Premer. They may be proven correct in time but Premer has been on campus for only two months.

In short, Carr, Williams, and Faison are the only certain skill position commodities. We will see who takes a step forward and if Denbrock can cobble together a diverse, dynamic attack.

Fortunately, the offensive line looks solid. It should create running lanes while also giving Carr time in the pocket. Ashton Craig is back at center following ACL surgery. Tackles Will Black and Guerby Lambert are large, athletic and physical players. Left guard Anthonie Knapp may be the best of the group. The only shuffling has occurred at right guard where Jagusah and Augustine are not available. Sullivan Absher played the position last season and should start on Sunday. He will be spelled by Owen Strebig, who had an impressive fall camp.

Wisconsin will counter with a defense geared toward stopping the run. Fickell imported two transfers at defensive tackle to shore up the middle. His sophomore linebackers, Mason Posa and Cooper Catalano, are studs. End Sebastian Cheeks provides juice in the pass rush and will test Black and Lambert. Both linebackers are capable blitzers who were productive as freshmen.

The Badger secondary is the largest question mark. Only safety Matthew Jung played in Madison last season. The other four starters are new transfers led by cornerback Javan Robinson from Arizona State. Notre Dame will attempt to take advantage of the fact that Sunday will be their first game together. Although the Irish are advertised as a run first team, I expect Denbrock to call more passes this season.

WISCONSIN'S OFFENSE vs. NOTRE DAME'S DEFENSE

Joseph is an exceptional athlete who starred for Old Dominion during the past two seasons. He ran for a pair of long touchdowns against Indiana and provides a dual threat to Wisconsin's attack. Joseph is a capable although not elite passer in terms of accuracy. He throws the deep ball well and more frequently than most college quarterbacks. Notre Dame's containment plan should mirror the strategy used against Taylen Green of Arkansas last season. The Irish contained him in the pocket and forced him to throw under duress. Chaos ensued for the Razorbacks.

Fickell also wants to reestablish the running game as a staple of Badger football. He brought in Sama to be his lead back. Although Sama lacks top end speed, he breaks tackles and is adept at finding a seam to run through. Wisconsin's best blockers are center Austin Kawecki and left tackle PJ Wilkins. Both are incoming transfers. If Mandell and Heywood are unable to play on the right side, the Badgers will likely run left. Joseph may also be running for his life.

Wide receiver is a huge question mark for this team. The starting trio of Tyrell Henry, Eugene Hilton, and Chris Brooks caught a combined 24 passes in 2025. Each of their backups is an incoming transfer that is still learning the playbook. Tight end Jacob Harris recorded 19 receptions and five touchdowns for Bowling Green last season. Nizyi Davis, a true freshman, backs up Harris.

Notre Dame's secondary has a significant advantage in this matchup, even if Shuler is not available. Wisconsin lacks proven weapons in the passing game and Joseph will be hard pressed to find open receivers. If the Irish can stay in man coverage, they will blitz Joseph from multiple angles. I would love to have Viliamu-Asa at full strength but Notre Dame probably will not need him. There are plenty of other players to watch on this defense. Ends Bryce Young and Boubacar Traore, along with freshman safety Joey O'Brien are on my list. At linebacker, both Drayk Bowen and Madden Faraimo are healthy after playing through nagging injuries in 2025.

Irish kicker Spenser Porath has been impressive in fall camp although he did have one poor scrimmage recently. Hopefully, he will be tested in this game and quell any concerns. Kicking issues have plagued the program over the past two years. It is time to turn a weakness into a strength.

Punter Jasper Scaife is a young Australian with a howitzer for a leg. Expectations that he can make it rain in Green Bay are high. The return and cover teams will be loaded with quality athletes. Faison and Greathouse will return punts while any one of the running backs could return kickoffs. As always, Notre Dame fans should pay attention when the Irish are in punt formation. Anything can happen.

Wisconsin has a veteran kicker in Gavin Lahm. The issue is that Lahm has been exclusively a kickoff specialist throughout his college career. He has never attempted a field goal or extra point in a game. Similarly, Badger punter Sean West has yet to attempt a punt in live action. Expect Notre Dame to exert maximum pressure in these moments. Henry, the starting slot receiver, is the primary return man for kickoffs and punts.

While Notre Dame has question marks at the offensive skill positions, the Badgers have a dearth of NFL level talent in this category. Joseph will have to play exceptionally well to put double-digit points on the board. This Irish defense has practiced against a very talented offense since March. They were challenged daily and acquitted themselves well. Wisconsin, by comparison, does not pose much of a threat other than the different looks they can provide.

Offensively, Notre Dame must find playmakers other than Williams and Faison. It is time for several players to make the leap from potential to production.

Wisconsin will strive to maintain a balanced attack by demonstrating the ability to run the ball. This task is made more difficult with two starters out on the right side of the offensive line. Still, running well is the only way the Badgers can make the contest competitive. Notre Dame's defense will feast on third and long situations and turnovers are likely to result.

Here are a few questions that will shed light on the outcome:

Will Notre Dame contain Joseph and force him into mistakes?

Which new Irish playmakers will emerge at tailback and receiver?

Will Carr demonstrate improved decision-making and passing accuracy?

Which team will control the line of scrimmage?

Will the Irish special teams contribute in a significant way?

Can Notre Dame's deep defensive line live up to its lofty expectations?

Will Notre Dame's secondary catch more passes than the Badger receivers?

Can the Irish demonstrate competency with the Lambeau Leap?

Freeman and Notre Dame have waited since November 29 of last year for this moment. Any baby conceived on or before that date has probably been born. Irish fans now eagerly anticipate the birth of a golden season with expectations not seen in decades. On Sunday we will begin to discover if those dreams are realistic. The journey will be long, however, with various ups and downs that are part of every football campaign. Players, coaches, and fans must focus on one opponent at a time to maintain equilibrium. After analyzing Sunday's matchup, I believe the Irish will pass this first test with flying colors.

Tell John what you think in the Comments section below.

Details about the design and release of Wembanyama's signature shoe have not been revealed.

articles.title: Two Champions. One Statement Game: No. 1 Ferris State Hosts Bentley Friday Night
articles.summary: Ferris State has not lost since 2024. Bentley is the NE10 champ picked to repeat, and it arrives in Big Rapids with nothing to lose. Friday night at Top Tagg...
articles.body:
There are regular-season games, and then there are measuring sticks.

When the top-ranked Bulldogs take the field Friday night at Top Taggart Field, they will be defending far more than a 31-game winning streak. They will be defending their place atop Division II football against a Bentley team that has already proved it belongs in the national conversation.

Kickoff is scheduled for 6 p.m. Friday, Sept. 4 , in Big Rapids. The two programs have never played each other.

Ferris State's Opener Was a 42-14 Warning

Ferris enters as the two-time defending national champion and the No. 1 team in the country. The Bulldogs wasted little time reminding Division II why last season ended with another trophy, dominating No. 4 Pittsburg State 42-14 in their season opener.

Ferris rushed for 385 yards while holding Pittsburg State to just 44 rushing yards . The Bulldogs produced 520 total yards and turned a 14-7 halftime lead into 28 unanswered second-half points .

Quarterback Wyatt Bower completed 12 of 17 passes for 135 yards and added 65 rushing yards and a touchdown. Senior running back Zak Ahern carried 12 times for 87 yards and two touchdowns.

It was a warning. And it came from a program that beat Harding 42-21 last December to claim its fourth Division II title in five years.

The Falcons are not entering Big Rapids as an overmatched opponent. Bentley went 7-3 in the regular season and 6-1 in Northeast-10 play last year, capturing its first conference championship since 2019 and earning its first NCAA playoff berth since 2021 . The Falcons were also picked to repeat as NE10 champions this season, taking five of the league's first-place votes.

Luke Warnock Gives the Falcons a Puncher's Chance

At the center of Bentley's hopes is quarterback Luke Warnock .

The NE10 Rookie of the Year in 2025 finished the final eight regular-season games with 22 touchdowns , including four rushing scores, while throwing only four interceptions during that span.

Bentley returns its top two running backs from last season, Telly Edouard and Joshua Compoh, who combined for 789 rushing yards . The Falcons also return an experienced defensive secondary and three All-NE10 defensive linemen in Jake Fredericks, Kieran Campbell and Quincy Pickett.

Ferris has the nation's longest active winning streak and already has a top-five victory this season. Bentley has a championship pedigree of its own and enters with nothing to lose. For Ferris, Friday is an opportunity to prove that the Bulldogs' dominance remains intact.

For Bentley, it is a chance to do something far more powerful: announce that the Falcons belong on the same field as the best team in Division II.

And for everyone else in the division, this game offers an early glimpse at what the road to the national championship could look like. One team is trying to stay on top, the other is trying to knock it off. That makes Ferris State-Bentley more than an early-September matchup.

articles.title: Defector set to launch new NFL podcast featuring Drew Magary, Arif Hasan, and no gambling
articles.summary: Defector, the worker-owned site built by the staff of Deadspin after it was gutted by private equity, is launching a new podcast to align with the start of t...
articles.body:
Defector, the worker-owned site built by the staff of Deadspin after it was gutted by private equity, is launching a new podcast to align with the start of the NFL season.

All Ball will feature Defector's Drew Magary and Arif Hasan, formerly of The Athletic and currently writing at Wide Left , talking about the world of professional football. In a trailer promoting the show, a voiceover promises potential listeners that it will feature "no fantasy talk, no gambling advice, and no other nerd s***."

"Drew and Arif are just two pure ball-knowers who only want to talk about one thing: football," the promo concludes.

In 2026, promising no gambling talk and no fantasy advice on a football podcast is actually a pretty strong zig against the zag of current trends. If a popular football show is not directly about gambling or fantasy, there's a good chance it's at least sponsored by a company that is profiting off of one of the two. It's just how things work now.

Hasan was on the Minnesota Vikings beat for The Athletic and continues to cover the team at Wide Left, and Magary is a die-hard Vikings fan, so while there will be no gambling, complaints and/or celebrations of Kyler Murray can likely be expected.

All Ball comes after the conclusion of Defector's previous flagship podcast, The Distraction , which ran its last episode last week . Magary and fellow Defector member David Roth hosted that show, which dates back to the Deadspin days when it was known as The Deadcast . Magary's new show will be taking over the old podcast feed.

articles.title: UNC football investigation: What to know about probe into allegations of drug use, 'sex between players, staff'
articles.summary: Here's the latest on the investigation into North Carolina football.
articles.body:
Under Bill Belichick, North Carolina has had a turbulent few years, and that continues with an investigation into two of Belichick's biggest confidants on his staff.

General manager Michael Lombardi and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick have been away from the team since the middle of the summer, and a new WRAL report says the two are part of a broader investigation into the program. Despite North Carolina's win over TCU in Week 0, the Tar Heels remain in hot water as the investigation continues.

Lombardi resigned from his position on Thursday, while Steve Belichick remains away from the team. Bill Belichick, meanwhile, marches forward as he coaches his second season in Chapel Hill.

Here's the latest on the investigation into North Carolina football.

WRAL News reports that the North Carolina football program is under investigation for several issues, including improper sexual relaionships and drug use within the football facilities.

The investigation appears to involve Mike Lombardi, who was general manager of the program before resigning on Thursday, and Steve Belichick, the defensive coordinator who is currently on medical leave, among others. The investigation is ongoing and includes broader allegations that stretch beyond Belichick and Lombardi.

Mike Lombardi resigned from his position as general manager of North Carolina football on Thursday amid the school's investigation into his conduct.

"I want to thank Chancellor Roberts and Bill Belichick for the opportunity to serve as the GM of UNC Football," Lombardi said in a statement released through his lawyer. "I have decided it's best for me to resign my position as GM to allow the team to focus on the '26 season."

It's unclear exactly what Lombardi was being investigated for, but WRAL News reports there are allegations of improper sex and drug use within the program. Additionally, lawyers reportedly asked about Lombardi's relationships and interactions with the players on the team.

As the general manager of the program, Lombardi is responsible for helping set the culture of the team, and any illegal or improper activities would be a poor reflection on his leadership. Lombardi's responsibilities included overseeing recruiting, and the recruiting staff is part of who is under investigation. MORE: Can Bill Belichick cool his hot seat at UNC?

Lombardi and Steve Belichick appear to be the main focuses of the investigation, per WRAL. Both Lombardi and Belichick went on leave around the same time, though for what appeared to be separate reasons.

Those are likely not the only two people being investigated, but they are the two biggest names connected to the probe and the only UNC employees named in the report. MORE: How much would it cost for UNC to fire Bill Belichick?

What questions are lawyers asking about Steve Belichick?

According to WRAL , lawyers have asked members of the North Carolina program about allegations that Steve Belichick used drugs at university facilities. Belichick has been on medical leave for the past month for an undisclosed reason.

Per the report, members of the program were asked not only about Belichick's alleged drug use, but also whether he provided drugs to at least one player on the team.

Steve Belichick has been on 'medical leave' since August 6 for an undisclosed reason, which included missing the team's opening game against TCU in Ireland last weekend. Bill Belichick acknowledged the leave before the game but said he couldn't expand on the situation.

"My son Steve is on medical leave," Belichick said before the game, via The Daily Tar Heel . "We look forward to getting him back as soon as possible. That's a medical situation, so I really can't make any further comment on that."

Prior to the 2025 season, North Carolina reportedly signed Steve Belichick to a two-year, $2.7 million deal to join the team as its defensive coordinator. According to WRAL , that makes him North Carolina's highest-paid assistant coach.

What questions are being asked about sex between UNC players, staff?

As part of the investigation, lawyers are also asking about improper sexual relationships within the program. According to WRAL, that includes the possibility of a relationship between a female recruiting staff member and a player, as well as possible improper relationships between assistant coaches and recruiting staff members.

It's unclear if Bill Belichick is being investigated himself, even though his program is under scrutiny. The WRAL reports currently name just Lombardi and Steve Belichick as the two main individuals under investigation at this time.

articles.title: Why Darlington Raceway Got The Name ‘The Lady in Black’
articles.summary: Darlington Raceway, one of NASCAR's oldest tracks, is known as "The Lady in Black."
articles.body:
Darlington Raceway is one of the oldest tracks on the NASCAR circuit. Opened in 1950, the 1.366-mile, egg-shaped oval has been a staple on the NASCAR schedule since the inaugural Southern 500 on Sept. 4, 1950, which was won by Johnny Mantz.

The Southern 500 at Darlington is one of NASCAR's crown jewel races along with the Daytona 500, Coca-Cola 600 and Brickyard 400. In addition to its prestigious, Darlington Raceway has earned the nicknames "The Track Too Tough to Tame" and "The Lady in Black."

For newer NASCAR fans, they may not be familiar with how the South Carolina track got its nickname. Here, we will look at how and why Darlington Raceway is known as "The Lady in Black"

'Lady in Black' nickname coined in 1965 column

In the leadup to the 1965 Southern 500, sportswriter Benny Phillips wrote a column on the Darlington Raceway, capturing how difficult it is to race around the treacherous speedway. Phillips compared the unpredictability of Darlington Raceway to Mata Hari, a German World War I spy.

In the column, Phillips wrote that Darlington Raceway is "as treacherous as Mata Hari… as unpredictable as any woman — these are the virtues of 'The Lady In Black.'"

Along with Phillips coining "The Lady in Black" nickname, it was also earned through Darlington's track features. Known for its dark track surface and black tire marks left by cars on the retaining walls, "The Lady in Black" fits in more ways than one.

Darlington Raceway stands out among other tracks in terms of its difficulty. Nearly every time NASCAR takes to Darlington, at least multiple cars have a few scrapes on the right side of their race cars due to contact with the outside wall.

The scratches, paint transfer and tire marks left on the cars are known as the "Darlington Stripe," commonly viewed as a badge of honor for racing at Darlington. Following a race at Darlington, the outside wall is often covered with black tire marks due to contact from the cars.

For multiple reasons, Darlington Raceway is known as "The Lady in Black" and will forever be one of the most historic racetracks NASCAR visits.

Darlington Raceway opens the Chase for 2026

"The Lady in Black" plays host to the first race of the 2026 Chase for both the Cup Series and the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series. On Saturday, the O'Reilly Series field will compete in the Fleetio 200 at 7:30 p.m. ET, while the Cup Series will run the Cook Out Southern 500 Sunday evening at 5 p.m. ET.

Darlington Raceway is the Chase opener for the second straight year, but will return to being the regular-season finale race in 2027, the first time since 2024.
